{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"issue","number":10936,"title":"Master: [redacted] test no longer finds an ordered guard after #10881 folds constant locals","body":"## Evidence

Run https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/actions/runs/42535743087 (head `[redacted]`), job `Rust ([redacted])`, step `Cargo nextest`.

`brokk-bifrost-flow scalar_state::tests::[redacted]` panics at `crates/bifrost-flow/src/scalar_state.rs:3421` with `inner comparison is normalized`. The test loops two sources at `scalar_state.rs:3402-3405`. The second source is `class C { boolean f() { int x = 1; if (x < 3) return true; return false; } }`. #10905 records literal-initialized int/long locals (`crates/bifrost-jvm-analysis/src/analyzer/java/semantic/values.rs:371`) and folds comparisons through `constant_truth` (`crates/bifrost-jvm-analysis/src/analyzer/java/semantic/control.rs:2271`), so `x < 3` becomes `ConstantBoolean { value: true }` and there is no `[redacted]` with constant 3 for the test to find. The first source, where `x` is a parameter and `x = 1` is an assignment, still produces the ordered guard and still exercises the original `be0eb46d6b9a` interval-replacement defect.

This test passed at run https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/actions/runs/42519603550 (head `[redacted]`, job `Rust ([redacted])`) before #10905 landed.

## Impact

Master Rust CI is red. The constant-folding behavior is intentional per #10905, so this is not evidence of a runtime regression, but the test no longer covers its stated defect for the second source.

## Next steps

Confirm the failing iteration is the second source. Update the test so the constant-local source asserts the folded `ConstantBoolean` guard (or use a non-constant local/initializer) while keeping the ordered-comparison and interval-feasibility assertions on the parameter/assignment source. If downstream flow is expected to retain an ordered guard even after exact constant folding, that needs an owner decision; current evidence points to intentional folding.

### Triage evidence

The test's second source uses an effectively final int local x = 1; #10905 now constant-folds `x < 3` to ConstantBoolean, so the [redacted](3) guard the test searches for is absent and the expect panics. The first parameter/assignment source still exercises the hardwon interval replacement.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"issue","number":10972,"title":"Rust: macro-derived operands from non-std macro crates are lowered without an identity check","body":"Part of #8386; follow-up to #10802; blocks #10930. Ruled a soundness gap by the native identity coordinator (2026-11-08).

## Problem

The structural producer gives path-qualified `log::{info, warn, error, debug, trace, log}!` the `log` runtime layout at parse time (`crates/bifrost-rust/src/format_args.rs`) and publishes `ExactMacroDerived`, which is globally complete argument coverage (`structural.rs` ~1908, `callable.rs:109`). Its operands then become ordinary semantic value flows (Rust `semantic.rs` ~11049-11210, `call_shape.rs:453`, `std_types.rs:2506`) with no identity check.

A `log::` path does not name the registry `log` package. It names whatever `log` resolves to: a manifest rename, a patched source, or a local `mod log` re-exporting a macro. Only #10802's conversion reader checks that identity, through `format_macro_dispatch`. So one question has two predicates, and generic IR consumers apply `format_args` semantics to arguments of a macro that may do something else.

## What is needed (shape ruled by the identity coordinator)

- One shared identity-admission gate for EVERY consumer of macro-derived operands from non-std macro crates.
- Parse time publishes a guarded CANDIDATE layout with an unresolved owner.
- Query time admits it through #10802's package reader, plus no shadowing local `macro_rules!` or import and no unknown glob import in scope. A refused call is `UnknownMacroDerived`.
- When the gate admits, answers equal today's. Cite a golden that shows no change for an ordinary `log::info!`.
- std's own macros (`format!`, `println!` and the rest) stay on the existing std identity path. Shadowing std is a documented limitation, not part of this fix.
- Expected levers: Rust ADAPTER_VERSION (the parse-time product changes from exact to candidate), the ICFG pair and a token. Send the design to the identity coordinator before building.

#10930 (bare `info!` after `use log::info`) then reuses the same candidate layout and gate.","author":"jbellis","url":"https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/issues/10972"}

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"pull_request","number":11028,"title":"Report failed workspace input sync as incomplete dependency evidence (#8357)","body":"Fixes #8357.

## What changed

When a language's workspace input sync failed, `dependency-evidence` answered as complete and untruncated:

- On a cold store, the language had no selected snapshot. `AnalyzerStore::[redacted]` iterated the snapshots that happened to be selected, so it skipped that language without a gap.
- On a warm store, the earlier revision stayed selected, and its stale rows answered for the changed checkout.

The analyzer already recorded the sync failure as `[redacted]`, but dependency reads never looked at it.

- `AnalyzerStore::[redacted](snapshots, language)` now looks up the analyzer language's own publishing key. A missing snapshot yields a `Missing` gap.
- `TreeSitterAnalyzer::[redacted]()` exposes the recorded failure. `[redacted]` returns it, and so does the Rust wrapper before its overlay path. RQL then emits its provider diagnostic with the store's message, and `MultiAnalyzer` turns it into a `Missing` gap.

The fix sits in shared reader and analyzer code, so it covers every publishing ecosystem. The producer is unchanged, so no cache identity lever moves.

## Validation

- New hard-won test `[redacted]` in `tests/suite_bench_policy/[redacted]`:
  1. A persisted build publishes a Cargo lock.
  2. The test inserts the next Rust revision into `workspace_revisions`, so the rebuild's sync fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed`. The fault is data because the cache checks its schema hash on open, so a planted trigger only forces a rebuild.
  3. After a lock edit, the query must not answer from the stale 1.0.0 selection and must carry the store error.
  
  Without the fix, the test fails at the stale-selection assertion.
- All 12 `[redacted]` tests pass. So do the store's `[redacted]` tests and the engine test `[redacted]`.
- Clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` is clean on bifrost-store, bifrost-analysis, bifrost-rust-analysis and bifrost-tools.
- `node scripts/[redacted]` passes.
- `slopcop check --base origin/master` reports 0 new findings.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"issue","number":11030,"title":"MCP startup blocks initialize on anonymous open-pack acquisition from GitHub","body":"## What happens

`bifrost --mcp <mode>` calls `[redacted]` (`src/bin/bifrost.rs`) before it serves the MCP transport. That call reaches `[redacted]` -> `discover_inventory` -> `UreqTransport::fetch` in `crates/bifrost-semantic-packs/src/download.rs`, which is an anonymous request to GitHub. Until the request returns, the server does not answer `initialize`.

## Evidence

- During GitHub's incident "Increased timeouts due to surge in anonymous users" (opened 2026-11-09 05:59Z), the release preflight step `scripts/public/[redacted]` timed out twice waiting 90 s for the `initialize` response, with empty stderr. The runs were release-gate [42571891848](https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/actions/runs/42571891848) on 4792246 and [42582737893](https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/actions/runs/42582737893) on e6ab07f. The same step passed at 698a44d before the incident, and no commit between those two points touches this path.
- Locally, a `--profile measure` build of master answers `initialize` immediately. With `HTTPS_PROXY` pointed at a blackholed address, it took about 18 s. A `sample` of the stalled process shows the main `bifrost-cli` thread in `bifrost::run_inner -> [redacted] -> [redacted] -> discover_inventory -> fetch_bytes`.

## Why it matters

Every MCP client start, such as Claude Code, Codex or an editor, waits on a network round trip to GitHub before the protocol handshake. A degraded or blocked network turns that wait into a client timeout, and the client cannot tell why. The release gate fails for a reason unrelated to the engine.

## Direction

Answer `initialize` without waiting on the network. Acquire the packs in the background, or on first use, and report pack availability through the existing completeness reporting until the packs are ready. Separately, the release compatibility smoke could pin its pack inputs so it does not depend on GitHub's anonymous API. Do that only as a test-hygiene measure, not as the fix.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"pull_request","number":11046,"title":"Rust workspace inventory reads are recorded and replayable (#10952)","body":"Fixes #10952. Part of #8386; relates to #7262 (F10).

## What changed

Rust workspace inventory queries on `RustFactSource` now record a replayable read key for each set-membership answer, including an empty answer. A retained policy unit whose answer depended on one of these sets is no longer reused after another file changes that set. The interim unattributed markers from #10970 are removed, so these products are reusable again.

Seven new `LookupKind`s, each registered in the read-key codec with strict decoding:

| Kind | Wrapper | Question | Readiness |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[redacted]` | `[redacted]` | trait spelling | topology and context complete |
| `[redacted]` | `[redacted]` | imported name | over-approximates |
| `[redacted]` | `[redacted]` | identifier spelling | over-approximates |
| `[redacted]` | `rust_trait_impl_rows` | placed trait declaration (blob, declaration, path) | topology and context complete |
| `[redacted]` | `[redacted]` | placed subject declaration | topology and context complete |
| `RustAliasBlobInventory` | `[redacted]` | alias spelling | over-approximates |
| `[redacted]` | `[redacted]` | macro naming | over-approximates |

- One selected-live reader, `store/rust_inventory.rs`, answers all seven over the snapshot's selected summaries, with a per-snapshot readiness memo. "Unavailable" stays distinct from "empty". The digest is computed over sorted, distinct projected rows. Each kind has its own digest domain.
- Kinds that count impls of a placed declaration require complete topology and reference context, and answer unavailable otherwise. They do not require summary completeness. Requiring it rejected ready hierarchy answers and broke 11 hierarchy tests. {"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"issue","number":11233,"title":"Rust context readers for macro-gated import routes and inactive cfg files read a gap detail shape that is no longer published","body":"Two Rust context readers cannot return a row on current publications, so the incompleteness reasons they report are never produced by these paths.

**Readers** (`crates/bifrost-store/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation/rust_crate_context.rs`, master 90d5a08170):

- `[redacted]` (reports `[redacted]`) joins on `json_extract(gap.detail, '$.member_blob')` and `json_extract(gap.detail, '$.declaration_id')` (lines 644-645).
- `[redacted]` (reports `InactiveCfgPlacement`) filters on `json_extract(gap.detail, '$.path')` and `json_extract(gap.detail, '$.activation')` (lines 680-687).

**Why they are dormant (confirmed by reading):** the publisher wraps every gap detail in an `evidence` array: `SQL_CR_GAPS_16` in `[redacted]:2290` selects `json_object('evidence', json_group_array(json(detail)))`, and `SQL_RUST_CRATE_GAPS_21` stores that value. The top-level keys `member_blob`, `declaration_id`, `path` and `activation` therefore do not exist, the extracts return NULL, and the joins and filters match nothing. Other readers in the same file iterate the array (`evidence.value`), for example lines 986-1000.

**Observed:** a real macro fixture returns zero rows from `[redacted]`. A synthetic fixture that supplies the old top-level shape does return rows.

**Unknown:** whether any answer is reported complete that should be incomplete. Another path may report the same gap (for example `[redacted]` does not read `gap.detail`). This needs a fixture with an import through a macro-gated module and one with a file under an inactive `cfg` placement, checked at the product surface.

**Decision needed when this is picked up:** repair the extraction (iterate `evidence`), which can change answers from complete to incomplete and so needs the ICFG pair; or delete the readers if another path already covers both cases.

Found while moving these readers onto unit-summary rows for #11173. That move keeps the current behavior and does not repair this.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"issue","number":11329,"title":"Python: a constructor call to a model-declared class never binds (dispatch unproven, coverage open), so typestate subjects on Class() are never selected","body":"## Summary

On the released Bifrost **v0.15.1** (build `[redacted]`, `packs/v0.11.0` bundle), a typestate subject selected at a Python constructor call never binds. A `resolved-call` to the model-declared `__init__` of a class leaves `call_bindings` with `dispatch outcome=unproven, coverage=open`, so every run is `inconclusive (partial_discovery)` and no automaton runs. That holds for a workspace class model and for the shipped, reviewed `ftplib.FTP.__init__` in `[redacted]`.

Python module functions bind fine with the same model shape (for example `venv.create(...)` and `webbrowser.open(...)` are `proven_by_summary` in taint policies), so the gap is specific to `Class(...)` calls.

Expected: `bz2.BZ2Decompressor()` (and `ftplib.FTP(host)`) resolves exactly to the declared `__init__`, binds its actuals, and its return value can be a typestate subject. If constructor dispatch cannot be proved, the run should say which proof is missing, but this is the case where the class and `__init__` are both declared.

## Minimal inert repro

`pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
name = "probe-348"
requires-python = ">=3.13.5, <3.13.6"
```

`reuse/main.py`:

```python
import bz2


def f(chunk, next_chunk):
    dec = bz2.BZ2Decompressor()
    try:
        dec.decompress(chunk)
    except OSError:
        pass
    return dec.decompress(next_chunk)
```

Workspace model `.bifrost/semantic-models/bz2.json` (schema 16): module `type.python.bz2`, class `[redacted]` (`bz2.BZ2Decompressor`, `[redacted]`), and two methods with `receiver: {pointer: false}` and `[redacted]`: `[redacted]` (`__init__()`, no parameters) and `[redacted]` (`decompress(data, max_length)`).

Policy: `:type typestate`, `:call-modeling (call-modeling :unmodeled require-model)`, subject

```
(resolved-call :resolves-to [redacted] :proof declared
  (call-bindings (call-shape (call :callee (name "BZ2Decompressor")))))
:subject return-value
```

and `decompress` events on the receiver at `before-call` and `[redacted]` (states `usable -> failed -> violated`).

Result for `reuse`, `fresh` (a new decompressor in the handler), `ok` (no try) and `reraise`:

```
completion: {"type": "inconclusive", "reasons": ["partial_discovery"], "scope": {"type": "run"}}
typestate selector did not execute completely: `/analysis/subjects/entries/decompressor/selector`
([redacted]: call_bindings did not establish complete actual-to-formal coverage
 (dispatch outcome=unproven, coverage=open, target_count=1, binding coverage=unknown))
```

Control with only shipped models (copy of `[redacted]` 0.7.0 in `.bifrost/semantic-models`), subject `[redacted]` on `ftplib.FTP(host)`, events on `[redacted]`:

```
[redacted]: call_bindings semantic model callable is incomplete: PartialModel;
[redacted]: call_bindings did not establish complete actual-to-formal coverage
 (dispatch outcome=unproven, coverage=open, target_count=1, binding coverage=unknown)
```

Using an exact qualified locator instead (`:resolves-to "[redacted]" :proof exact`) gives the same result with the model, and `not_run` / `[redacted]` without it (compare #5240 for `ssl.SSLContext.__init__`).

The full probe (models, policies, cases) is in BrokkAi/bifrost-packs under `research/osv-dataflow-2026-11/python/probe/348-bz2-typestate`.

## Impact

This blocks every Python typestate policy over a library object created by its constructor. It is the engine blocker (after CPython version evidence, #3867) for BrokkAi/bifrost-packs#348 and #349 (decompressor reuse after an error) and BrokkAi/bifrost-premium-packs#602 (Pillow image reuse after `DecompressionBombError`). {"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"pull_request","number":11356,"title":"ci-fix: Walk Go expression wrappers without recursion","body":"Fixes #11351.

## What changed

`LoweringContext::[redacted]` in `crates/bifrost-go-analysis/src/analyzer/go/semantic.rs` now unwraps nested `[redacted]` nodes with the shared `[redacted]` helper and walks unary `&`/`*` wrappers in the same loop. Pointer-depth changes are applied innermost first, preserving the previous checked address/dereference behavior.

The new regression test `[redacted]` lowers the 512-parenthesis receiver fixture on a 1 MiB thread stack. It aborts on the old recursive implementation and passes with the iterative walk.

## Why

Release gate https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/actions/runs/42781452370 (job 129721471580, `[redacted]` 4 of 4) failed only on this test:

```
thread 'bifrost-parse-0' has overflowed its stack
fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
```

`[redacted]` recursed once per nested parenthesis. On x86_64 its debug frame is 3,048 bytes, so 512 levels use about 1.5 MiB of the 2 MiB parse-worker stack before caller frames. AArch64's larger frames crossed the limit. Tree-sitter parsing is iterative; the overflow was in Go semantic lowering during `[redacted]`.

Reproduced on x86_64 at `57abda3e14f` by constraining the process to `RUST_MIN_STACK=1048576`: the existing test aborts on `bifrost-parse-0` with the same message. The new regression test also aborts on the recursive version.

## Introducing commit

No commit in the first-red range `15a2118348..b7ccdd35` changed this walk: `semantic.rs` has blob `63255c61f0e` at both endpoints and at current master `57abda3e14f`, and the parse-worker plumbing is unchanged. The red run is a stack-headroom threshold crossed on aarch64, not a causal code change. The recursive walk predates the range, so this is a FIX that removes the depth-proportional recursion rather than a REVERT of an unrelated change.

## Validation

- `RUST_MIN_STACK=1048576` x86_64 reproduction: old code aborts in `bifrost-parse-0`; fixed code passes the existing `[redacted]` test.
- `[redacted]=1 eatmydata cargo nextest run -p [redacted] --lib --max-fail 100`: 321/321 passed.
- `eatmydata cargo clippy -p [redacted] --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed file: passed.

## Limitations

- No aarch64 Linux runner is available in this container; the aarch64 frame-size crossing is inferred from the x86_64 constrained-stack reproduction and the reported abort. The named release-gate test is the one validated.
- The fix bounds the transparent wrapper walk (parentheses and unary address/dereference). It does not change other Go semantic resolution code.

Agent: The slice 1b child stopped on its upgrade test. The fault was in the test's simulation of an old store, not in production.

**Why the test failed.** To fake a version-24 store, the test changed only the stored version number. A summary's digest includes its derivation version (`unit_summaries.rs` around line 1373). So a real version-24 summary has a different digest, which the new binary cannot match, and it re-derives. Changing only the number left a summary that still looked current, so nothing re-derived.

**What I did**
- **Committed the work so far** as a checkpoint (bca1830a2c): the writers, the lifecycle cleanup, the version bump to 25, the differential checks and the explicit column fixes. The store suite passed on this code: 1,190 tests in the dev profile.
- **Started a child** to make the simulation faithful: change both the version and the digest, clear the new rows, then reopen. If it still does not re-derive, the child stops and reports, since that would be a real defect. It then runs the remaining validation: the Rust engine tests and goldens, Clippy, the workspace build and the checks.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The child was right to stop. "Reopen does not re-derive" could have meant either a broken upgrade path or a wrong test. The code settles it: the digest includes the version, so reuse cannot happen across a version change. A faithful simulation has to change what the old binary would actually have written, not just the field that looks relevant.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"issue","number":11402,"title":"Rust: a mutating method on an owned local loses the receiver write (false negative reported complete)","body":"Found while implementing #11299 (umbrella #8386). Measured on #10930's head a41c03bc7e, unchanged.

```rust
let mut buffer = String::new();
buffer.push_str(password);        // test summary: arg0 flows into the receiver
vector_sink(buffer);              // expected: a finding
```

This produces NO finding, and the result is reported COMPLETE (`ProvenBySummary`, no diagnostics). The authored arm closures list the push_str transfer summary, so the summary is applied, but its write to the receiver never reaches `buffer`. It is a false negative with a complete status. The same holds for `write!(buffer, ...)`, which expands to `buffer.write_fmt(...)`.

Cause (by reading the code): in rust `semantic.rs` call_expression (about 12335-12341) an owned method receiver is lowered as `expression_value(receiver, expression_value_kind(receiver))`, which for an identifier is a plain Temporary value with no Address. The `&mut` write-back loop (about 12493-12520) writes callee effects back to the place only for arguments, never for the receiver. So a callee summary that writes `self` updates a temporary copy.

What is needed: when the receiver is a place expression and the callee may write its receiver (a `&mut self` method, or an unknown receiver mode), apply the same write-back to the receiver's place that `&mut` arguments get. Unknown cases stay conservative. This must agree with #11272's local identity work (explicit Address plus LexicalCell for explicitly borrowed locals; session 1bb01cc7), which does not cover receiver autoref. Regression: the snippet above gives a finding. Policy goldens that gain true findings are blessed with this cause; any lost finding is a stop.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"issue","number":11428,"title":"PHP: `new` of a class declared in another file always records an Unknown destructor-timing gap, making the procedure's taint inconclusive","body":"## Summary

In PHP, any `new C()` where `C` is declared in a different file records an Unknown `ResourceManagement` gap, "object destructor timing and resource lifetime are not lowered". That makes the whole enclosing procedure's taint `inconclusive`, even when `C` is a `final` class with no supertype, interface, trait or `__destruct`, and even when the allocated object has nothing to do with the flow.

When #9329 was closed, the comment listed this as still open after #9411 ("`new` of any class declared outside the file still raises PHP lowering's object destructor timing gap"), but no issue tracks it. It blocks almost every third-party PHP rule, because application code gets library objects from `new` (`new PHPMailer()`, `new Client()`, `new Browsershot()`, `new CsvEncoder()`).

## Repro (released v0.15.1, build `90d820b9`, vendor route)

The vendor stub `vendor/codeigniter4/framework/system/HTTP/Files/UploadedFile.php` declares `final class UploadedFile` with `move(string $targetPath, string $name): bool` and `getClientName(): string`, plus a PSR-4 `vendor/composer/installed.json`. The policy is taint from `getClientName()` return to `move` argument 1, both `resolved-call :proof exact`. Open packs and downloads are off.

| Probe | `store()` body | Completion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `param` | `store(UploadedFile $file)`: `$file->move('/srv/uploads', $file->getClientName());` | complete, 1 finding |
| `new-vendor` | `$file = new UploadedFile(); $file->move('/srv/uploads', $file->getClientName());` | **inconclusive** (finding kept, partial): "procedure semantics for … Upload.store is unknown" |
| `new-vendor-unrelated` | `param` body plus an unused `$other = new UploadedFile();` | **inconclusive** (finding kept, partial), same |
| `new-samefile` | `param` body plus `$holder = new Holder();` where `final class Holder {}` is in the same file | complete, 1 finding |

Probe inputs are committed in BrokkAi/bifrost-premium-packs under `research/validation/probes/php-cve-catalog-0151/new-expression/`.

## Cause (read from source, not built)

`crates/bifrost-php-analysis/src/analyzer/php/semantic.rs` on `origin/master` records the gap unless `[redacted](node)`. That check looks the class up in `self.classes`, which holds only the classes this file declares, so any class from another workspace file, the vendor tree or a semantic model counts as open.

## Expected

Decide the lifetime from the class's resolved declaration, wherever it is declared: a workspace or vendor class whose full declaration is known to have no `__destruct` on it or any ancestor (final, or with a closed hierarchy), and a semantic-model class that declares or proves the same. Keep the gap for classes whose hierarchy or destructor is unknown. At minimum, an allocation whose value doesn't reach the tracked flow shouldn't make an unrelated flow's procedure unknown.
","author":"DavidBakerEffendi","url":"https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/issues/11428"}

Resolve the formal's AST component and rank into `JavaConversionType`, then use the same classifier as the actual argument. Matching primitive and nominal arrays can now publish identity conversions; incompatible primitive components, rank mismatches, and unresolved component types still refuse with their typed causes.

Fixes #11424. This is the prerequisite for #11296's conditional family conversion work. It adds no object-identity or ownership proof and changes no published IR or adapter format. The ICFG pair rotates together, and the assigned `[redacted]` policy component is included conservatively because complete answer-digest coverage across all policy consumers has not been proved.

Validated in DEFAULT DEV at effective nice 10: the nine-case ordinary/native regression, 14 conversion tests, 20 JVM AST/classifier tests, 69 native Java tests, identity pins, and Java/JVM-focused goldens. The Python typed golden passes isolated nextest; its shared-process numbering failure is tracked in #6425. Touched-crate all-target Clippy, formatting, and pack drift checks pass. The own regression passes again after the pre-PR master merge at `[redacted]`, which has a clean mj review.

The corrected shared B1a r5 gate is pending. This PR stays draft until the final no-JDK and pinned-JDK comparison is accepted, with every intentional ordinary-array answer change attributed.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"pull_request","number":11557,"title":"Write no PDB for the Windows semantic-pack lib test link","body":"The release gate's Windows rust build fails in **Semantic pack distribution tests** with `LNK1318: Unexpected PDB error; LIMIT (12)`. The failure happens while linking the `[redacted]` lib test (`--features download`). It reproduced on two gate runs of `candidate/v0.15.2-rc`, on the same `[redacted]`, and it blocks the v0.15.2 release. Master's gates have the same step. They haven't reached it on Windows since Nov 9, because clippy failures and spot interruptions stopped them first.

## Cause
MSVC 14.44 rejects any PDB symbol name over 64 KiB. This lib test links the whole analysis stack, and Rust's legacy mangling of its deeply generic symbols now exceeds that limit (rust-lang/rust#141626).

## Change
- On the Windows target only, this step sets `[redacted]=symbols`. rustc then links with `/DEBUG:NONE`, so no PDB is written.
- Panics still report their message and location.
- Release builds already strip symbols, so they are not affected.
- The nextest archive keeps its line tables for hang diagnostics.
- Other targets are unchanged.
- The step now runs in bash so it can export the variable conditionally.

## Validation
- `actionlint` passes on the workflow.
- `scripts/[redacted]` passes 51 of 51. The step's command assertion was updated, and a new assertion pins the Windows strip.
- `node scripts/[redacted]` passes, and SlopCop is clean.

Once this lands, it will be cherry-picked onto `candidate/v0.15.2-rc`. The longer-term fix is v0 symbol mangling, which keeps symbols and also covers the archive step. That changes RUSTFLAGS, so it isn't part of this release fix.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"pull_request","number":11571,"title":"Repair legacy 325 stores on the non-rebuild migration pass (#11564)","body":"## What changed

`migrate_locked` now runs the legacy-F repair whenever a store reports schema 325 or later and the repaired migrations (0315, 0316, 0323) sort below its `user_version`, not only during the `rebuild_invalid_schema` pass at the current version. A store already at the current version still repairs only on the rebuild pass, so foreign keys remain disabled for every repair.

## Why

Migration 0334 (merged by `03bfe0c62a9`, PR #11519) deletes from tables created by 0323, including `[redacted]`. A pre-publication schema-325 F store that skipped 0315/0316/0323 lacks that table. The public `migrate` path calls `migrate_locked(..., false)` with `user_version == 325`; the old gate required the rebuild pass at `[redacted]`, which is now 334, so the repair never ran and 0334 aborted.

Tolerating the missing table inside 0334 would not work: the migration deletes from several 0323 tables and the final schema must still contain them, so the store would fail `[redacted]`. The repair is the established legacy-store path (#11229) and must run on the non-rebuild pass. That pass is safe because `migrate` disables foreign keys whenever `user_version` is below the current version.

Introducing merge: `03bfe0c62a9` (PR #11519). Its parent `601bd53b018` passes both tests; `03bfe0c62a9` and the repair base `d786fbe087c` fail them.

Failing run: https://github.com/BrokkAi/bifrost-dev/actions/runs/42891205016, job 130101489074, at `[redacted]` (Windows rust-all).

## Validation

Before the change at `d786fbe087c`:

```
[redacted]="${[redacted]}" eatmydata cargo nextest run -p brokk-bifrost-core --lib legacy_325_store --max-fail 10
```

At `03bfe0c62a9` (introducing merge): the same 2 tests fail with the same error. At parent `601bd53b018`: 2 passed.

After the change at `d26969c4d7a`:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed.

Limitations: the full Windows rust-all job was not run locally. The unrelated `resolution_schema::[redacted]` failure from the same run is tracked by #11565 and fixed by #11569; it is not part of this change.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"issue","number":11609,"title":"Measure the per-request Go membership rebuild on a large repository before designing retention (#11482 follow-up)","body":"## Question

#11482 records Go package membership as a selection-authority read. One owner function, `[redacted]`, hashes each selected domain's canonical package and file rows. It is memoized per request, and replay calls the same function. After review (1b2eb7f142), a request with no ordinary capture and no evaluation skips the computation entirely. A request that records authorities still rebuilds the whole-workspace membership once per request: a policy evaluation, or a query running under a read capture.

Measure that per-request rebuild on a large Go repository (many domains and thousands of package/file rows) against evaluation time and warm-request time. The only measurement so far is 1.9 ms per evaluation on the xcrypto fixture (1 domain, 23 rows). That fixture is too small to show how the cost grows, so it is not evidence either way for large repositories.

## Only if the cost matters

Design cross-request retention. A cached membership answer is sound only if every writer of the membership rows either mints a new publication or bumps a generation that the cache key includes. Refresh (#11198) and repair (#11515) can change rows under an existing publication today. That is why the coordinator rejected a stored membership digest. So retention first needs a writer audit across those paths, with a trigger or a test that proves the property. Without that proof, a cache would replay stale membership.

Follow-up to #11482 (native-engine coordinator ruling, 2026-11-10).

This is a capability follow-up, separate from restoring the two lost anonymous written-signature proofs tracked by #11562.

The permanent public family `tests/fixtures/golden/call-bindings/[redacted]/main.go` defines `type F func() error`, `type Pair func() (int, error)`, assigns unknown function parameters into package variables, and calls them. At source commit `[redacted]`, the exported `[redacted]` proof is unknown for `named()` at lines 24 and 34 and `pair()` at line 28. Both the retired AST proof and the exact current-local before control are also unknown. These three cases remain explicit unchanged controls; no legacy fallback is retained for them.

The controlled full comparison covers 1,729 calls over 185 roots and 335 Go files: all seven anonymous/grouped/written-signature migration gaps close, with 45 equal-positive and 1,684 both-unknown rows. Every noncandidate outcome and operational cause equals the current-local before control. This evidence does not establish support for named package function types. The public before/after captures on identical expanded input preserve all RQL results and all 17 canonical identities; parameter controls with named function types already have canonical identities, while these package globals do not.

The approved observation-only check on 2026-11-11 identifies the existing declared-type stage as the decisive stop. Both global binders pass syntax eligibility, complete declaration lookup and exact declaration matching. Their declared-type results are `Incomplete` with `incomplete_native_type` and `UnsupportedSemantic` at `main.go:7:5` and `main.go:10:5`; the existing `explicit_binding_type` status check returns empty unless the result is `Resolved` (`crates/bifrost-go-analysis/src/analyzer/go/native_points.rs:2800-2802` at `[redacted]`). That predicate predates this binding slice. Named parameter controls resolve successfully. The observer passed complete OFF/ON rendered-primary and returned-work equality and both normal golden runs. The deeper source of `UnsupportedSemantic` is not attributed by this check. Investigate that declared-type capability using the existing selected source and binding authority. Do not infer a producer defect from this result, normalize unknown to complete, add a name search or AST scope walker, derive the type from an initializer body, or preserve a legacy path. Review the concrete plan with the native-engine coordinator before changing resolution. A std or core `matches!` call is not a call: when its identity is proven, it is now realized as an intrinsic match with no call. Step 1 (#11541, landed) added the shared `standard_macro_identity`. This PR depends on #11360 M2 (#11603, head 091120612e) and targets that branch, so the diff shows only step 2.

## What changed

- **Candidate records.** A candidate macro invocation is identified by its source anchor, the base call it replaces and a typed realization in the alternate: `RuntimeCall(alternate call)`, `Intrinsic` (no call) or `[redacted]` (the shape agreed for #11532). The anchor is a lookup index within one blob's artifact. Digests, receipts and read keys identify a candidate by its position-free base call, so raw offsets never enter a digest. One validator (`[redacted]`) serves IR construction and the Rust lowering assertion. RuntimeCall needs the alternate call to exist; Intrinsic needs no call at the anchor; a lexical guard keeps the base call.
- **Storage.** Migration 0371 (`[redacted]`, classified breaking) rebuilds `[redacted]` with `anchor_start`, `anchor_end`, `base_call`, `realization` (CHECK in `call`, `intrinsic`, `[redacted]`) and `alternate_call`, which is NOT NULL exactly when the realization is `call`. These are rows, not a blob. Old rows cannot supply anchors, and the IR version bump keeps old heads off them.
- **Lowering.** Rust lowers `matches!` as an opaque candidate call in the base procedure and as an intrinsic in the guarded alternate. The alternate uses the shared match-arm pattern helper, including `pat if guard`, and produces a fresh non-dropping Boolean.
- **Admission.** The whole alternate is selected only when every candidate admits. An Intrinsic admits only when `standard_macro_identity` proves `Standard { member: "matches" }`, including the enclosing wrapper for nested calls such as `assert!(matches!(..))`. Otherwise the identity is refused and the candidate row keeps its #11260 reason:
  - a local `macro_rules! matches`;
  - a `#[macro_use] mod`;
  - a glob import;
  - a `#[macro_use] extern crate` whose crate exports a `matches` (a `macro_rules!` or a crate-root `#[proc_macro]`);
  - a `#[macro_use] extern crate` with no indexed source, because its exports cannot be listed.

  The last case also makes other standard-prelude macros in that file, such as `println!`, read `Unknown(Unresolved)`. That is the sound answer.
- **Call shapes and RQL.** `[redacted](anchor)` returns RuntimeCall, Intrinsic or NotAdmitted. Call-shape and binding projection drop the row for an admitted Intrinsic, keep the refused candidate row with its reason, and refine RuntimeCall to the alternate call. Parse time suppresses nothing.

Each value was assigned by the coordinators and is rechecked at the final merge:

| Lever token lines | `11251-matches-intrinsic` in `[redacted]` and `policy-substrate.tokens` (after #11654; the numbered pair v945/v944 is retired) |
| Rust store salt | `[redacted]` |
| Migration | 0371 (first 0337, then 0342 and 0359; after master landed 0361, the coordinator moved it above M2's 0370) |

The Rust store salt stays, because Rust structural output changes for unchanged bytes. A `matches!` with native operands now publishes call-shape coverage `candidate_macro_derived`, where it was `unknown_macro_derived`, and guarded operands now parse.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"pull_request","number":11701,"title":"Stop a parent scope's proof stop from dropping taint sources","body":"Fixes #11662. A regression from the Rust proof-stop change (f3fffc13b7): an operational proof stop recorded in one part of a request became the incompleteness of every later query in that request. In taint policies, the sink phase's stop made the source selectors' queries Incomplete. The incomplete-selector filter then dropped every literal, identifier and field source row without a diagnostic. In #11662 an unrelated finding disappears when another procedure, earlier by name, reads a tuple field in a sink.

## What changed

- **Reasons propagate up only.** `[redacted]` copied a parent scope's sticky execution-dependent reason into each child scope as the child's own reason. It is removed. A scope now reports only the reads it made, and they still reach its ancestors. Master's `IndependentAnswer` boundary (#11550) was an early return inside that function, so it goes too. #11539's `[redacted]` still holds. Removing the marker, which no longer changes anything, is #11679.
- **Syntax-identity source rows stay possible sources.** When a taint selector's discovery is Incomplete, the filter kept only call-binding, decorated-parameter and keyed-read rows (`usable_taint_row`'s `_ => false`, from #3732). Rows whose identity is the AST node (literal, identifier, field) are now kept as possible endpoints marked Unproven/Partial. Rows that are still withheld are counted in the selector's typed incompleteness, so nothing is dropped without a diagnostic. For example, the `field-write-port` golden now reports `0 syntax-identity rows ..., 4 rows withheld ...: {FieldWriteValue: 4}`.
- **Request-local values replay their completion** through `CompletedMemoValue` and `MemoCompletionReceipt`, so a cache fill that consumes a failed request-local value is refused.

## Performance result (measured by 85e2d8a9 on 3b5d256f89)

On the Tantivy unit `set_block/tests.rs`, whose real-code runs hit the 2-hour stop:

| Counter | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RustFileRoutes` memo hits | 0% | 99.999% |
| Route SQL statements | 67,021 | 8 |
| Receipts | 109,695 uncacheable | 6,219, all cacheable |
| Unit time | more than 22 minutes | 33 s |

The cause was the same inheritance. OpenBoundary and UnsupportedSemantic stops are Provider stops. Through inheritance they made the whole request execution-dependent, so `memoized_route_index` refused to publish. On Bat (#11599), the cold run's SQL halves, but it still publishes no units. The 32 unusable receipts and 18 provider rows left there are a separate lever, outside this PR's scope.

## Tests

Each regression pin below was run on a variant with the fix reverted and failed there, and passes on the fix:
- analysis: `[redacted]` (it also asserts that a unit scope under a stopped parent keeps a clean ledger), `[redacted]`, `[redacted]`;
- policy: `[redacted]` (hard-won), which fails with only the propagation change reverted, and `[redacted]`, which fails with only the row-retention change disabled;
- golden: `[redacted]` (#11662), whose `aaa_case` loses its finding on the reverted variant.

`[redacted]` also passes on the reverted variant, because at fixture scale the stop does not reach the source selectors. It stays as a guard, without a hard-won tag.

`[redacted]` (rust-analysis cargo_routes.rs, hard-won for the #11599 real-code stops) checks the route memo. An unrelated earlier read in the request stops operationally; the route build reads none of it, so its memo publishes and a second consumer hits it. It fails with the inheritance added back by hand.

The seam profile can now show that every JVM selected-resolution operation reported its reads, and it tells a known-empty operation apart from one that never reported.

- `crates/bifrost-store/src/analyzer/resolution/seam_profile.rs`:
  - The request counter `in_flight` becomes a `Mutex<OperationLedger>`: open requests, a request `seq`, an operation counter and completions. An operation's id and its attribution must be decided together, so one critical section takes both. The close snapshot is therefore exact.
  - Each request line gains `seq` and `"jvm_operations": {"first", "next", "completed"}`. The operations that opened while the request was open are the ids in `[first, next)`.
  - Each operation line is `{"kind":"jvm_operation_reads","op":<id>,"status":...,"reads":[...]}` plus one attribution field decided when the operation opened: `"request": <seq>` when exactly one request was open, `"unattributed": true` when none was, and `"overlapped": true` when several were.
  - The earlier of two overlapping requests now also reports `overlapped: true`. Before, only the later one did, although both requests' counter deltas include the other's work.
- `crates/bifrost-store/src/analyzer/store/resolution_operation.rs`: the one profile constructor decides which operations are inventoried: a selection with a JVM language (Java, Kotlin, Scala) while the seam profile is on. Widening to other languages is that one predicate.
- `.../resolution_operation/jvm_context.rs`: `JvmContextReadProfile::open` takes the id. `Drop` always writes one line: `reads: []` for a known-empty operation, and status `panicked` when the drop runs during unwinding (partial reads).
- `.agents/scripts/jvm-gate/[redacted]` runs its self-test first (CI does not run it), then validates each capture before pairing:
  - operation inventory: `missing`, `unfinished`, `duplicate`, `misattributed`, `unmatched` (a process killed mid-request leaves these), `[redacted]`, `failed_collection`, `malformed_record`, `[redacted]`, `request_count_differs`;
  - answer alignment: request `seq` values must be dense from 0 (`request_seq_gap` otherwise). The recorded answers are the last requests, the answered priming attempt is the one before them, and earlier requests are readiness retries, reported as `readiness_retry` and left out of pairing. Anything that does not align fails as `[redacted]`;
  - stops: a request whose answer, priming or recorded, shows a stop (`incomplete_reason` `cancelled` or `time_budget`, the diagnostic kinds that map to them, or `"cancelled": true`) is a failed collection. Its operations are reported and never compared, because a stop can leave partial reads under a `completed` status;
  - `--expected-requests N` requires an exact alignment and N recorded answers.

  Unattributed and empty operations are reported (`SEAM_REPORTED`) and do not fail; an empty operation is exempt from the one-`demand_provider` rule.
- `.agents/scripts/jvm-gate/[redacted]` records every priming attempt, with its answer or error, in `priming.json`.
- `.agents/scripts/jvm-gate/README.md` documents the fields and classes.

## Decisions and limits

- Pairing across captures. Point lookups open their operation on the calling thread (`native_points.rs:909`), but graph and worker-pool operations open concurrently on rayon threads (`worker_transport.rs:212`), so the order of ids differs between runs. The id is therefore used only for completeness. Pairing is by request rank in `seq` order, comparing each request's operations as an unordered collection. - Operations outside requests. Only the two MCP tool paths open a seam request scope (`rmcp_host.rs`). A JVM operation opened from the CLI, a test or another path is `unattributed`, never counted inside a request range.

{"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"pull_request","number":11720,"title":"Reuse verdict M3 (analysis): return verdicts from the bifrost-analysis producers","body":"Milestone 3, item 7 (first half) of `.agents/plans/[redacted]`, for #10872: the `bifrost-analysis` producers return or join an explicit `ReuseVerdict` next to the ambient mark they keep (dual write). The hooks half is the stacked follow-up PR.

## What changed
- **Capture boundaries.** `[redacted]` and `[redacted]` accept the computation's verdict. They join it into the captured ledger before it is forwarded, so the shadow comparison sees it at that capture and at every enclosing capture.
- **Producer helpers in `i_analyzer`.**
  - `execution_dependent(analyzer)` marks ambiently and returns `ExecutionDependent(Other)`.
  - `[redacted](analyzer)` also joins that verdict through `join_reuse_verdict`. It is for producers whose result is a shared cached product or a value read by another crate. It takes the same analyzer route as the ambient mark, so the explicit verdict reaches exactly the ledgers the mark reaches.
- **`statement_entries`.**
  - `ProcedureSyntax::prepare` returns a typed `ProcedureSyntaxOpen` that carries its verdict.
  - `[redacted]` returns `(assessments, verdict)`. The tree-sitter memo builds it under `[redacted]`.
- **`derived_cache`.** `ensure_forward_inner` returns a `ForwardResolution` that carries the verdict of its byte-budget and omitted-file refusals, and `[redacted]` gains a `reuse` field.
  - These sites mark through core's frame route. With no frame on the thread, that route reaches no ledger, while `join_reuse_verdict` falls back to every active context. Joining there could therefore make the explicit verdict stricter than the ambient one, so the verdict stays in the value.
  - The boolean `ensure_forward*` APIs keep their signatures because their rql caller is out of scope.

Memoize `selected_external_route` per request so the Rust `?` residual-conversion proof (and the three other callers) stop reopening a selected operation and recomputing the macro frontier for the same written type heads. Fixes #11710.

Based on ed65adc0e2 (head of `[redacted]`, PR #11701, master 08e4dc8aa9 merged); this PR targets that branch so the review shows only this change. Prerequisite head built on: [redacted] (The parent has since moved; I merge it before marking ready.)

## What changed
- `RustRouteRequestMemo` gets a `selected_routes` memo (`rust/mod.rs`), filled through the existing `memoized_route_index` machinery. Key: file path, source length plus SHA-256 digest (no copy of the file), node kind, byte range. Value: `Selected`, `LocalDefinition` or `Rejected`. `Unavailable` is never published; a fill with execution dependences is not published; a hit replays the fill's receipt. A cancelled caller is not served a published answer.
- Bounds: 8,192 fill attempts per request (past it no new key is admitted, published answers are still served); a same-key re-entrant fill builds unmemoized instead of parking on its own cell.
- `KeyedPoolSafeMemo::existing_cell` (read-only lookup that never creates a cell).
- Nothing persisted changes. No lever token.

## Known remainder
The `?` check's `RustTypeProof` opens its own selected operation per check for `callee_definition` and `workspace_definition` lookups. That is about 15% of the check's macro-frontier recomputes and is not touched here (it is private to the check; sharing it is a separate change). Also separate: letting the retained macro frontier survive a deterministic `Incomplete` answer.

## Request memo storage
The new memo has the same lifecycle as its siblings in `RustRouteRequestMemo` (dies with the outermost scope, no retention regions). A reviewer asked for accounted request-private regions; moving the whole family onto regions is a separate change.

## What changed

Core #11451 added `LimitedCounter::try_allow`/`try_charge`. They return a `LimitRefused` that carries `ExecutionDependent(Other)`. Core kept `allows`/`charge` as bool wrappers. This PR moves every remaining sibling caller to `try_allow`.

**Scope.** All the callers are in rql: 54 sites in 12 files under `structural/search/`.
- The go, cpp, jvm, rust and policy crates never call `LimitedCounter` directly. Their limits run through core's `ResolutionSession` and `[redacted]`, which #11451 already moved.
- `bifrost-store` (`import_graph.rs`) and `bifrost-python-analysis` (`hierarchy.rs`) also call it, but they were outside this card's list and are left for a follow-up.
- The bool wrappers stay until Milestone 4.

**Where each refusal's verdict goes.** I traced each site's refusal through its callers. There are three kinds of site.
- **51 sites change only spelling.** Their refusal already becomes a value that the query's verdict reads:
  - a truncation flag that the query close turns into `QueryExecutionState::[redacted]`;
  - a budget diagnostic whose `reuse_verdict()` is non-Content;
  - a cache `reuse` that `cache_reuse` folds;
  - a typed gap, such as `ScalarConditionGap::WorkLimit` or `Incompleteness::Operational(Budget)`, that a caller joins.
- **`PipelineOutputLimit::allows_next` had no route.** Four of its callers stop producing rows with a bare `break` and set no flag, so nothing carried the refusal. `allows_next` now joins the refusal's verdict into the step's `reuse` sink. The identical-captures and call-bindings steps now take that sink from the dispatcher, as `[redacted]` already did. Row output is unchanged.
- **Fair-seed lease admissions.** The two in `mod.rs` called `allows(0)` only for its ambient mark. They now count the refused lanes and assert that at least one refused. Every consumer of the rejection already truncates and pushes a budget diagnostic.

The bare `break` at `allows_next` looks like an existing gap, apart from the verdict. When a step's output reaches `max_pipeline_rows`, the remaining input rows are dropped without setting the step's `exhausted` flag. Today only the ambient mark records the dependence. {"repo":"brokkai/bifrost-dev","kind":"pull_request","number":11840,"title":"A never-satisfiable cfg-gated mod emits no placement gap (#11786)","body":"Fixes #11786.

## What changed

The Rust source producer emitted an `[redacted]` gap for every cfg-gated, file-backed `mod name;`. The store lowers that gap to a lexical fallback row at the enclosing scope head, and no Rust path discharges it. As a result, every unqualified lookup in that scope was `Incomplete`, including lookups that have nothing to do with the module, such as the imported alias head in the issue's example.

The producer now skips that gap when the module's predicate can never be satisfied under any atom set, for example `#[cfg(any())]` or `#[cfg(not(all()))]`. Such a module can never be active, so it cannot shadow or place anything. The module is still lowered (binder, export, `UnprovenActivation` on the declaration), so references through it keep their typed diagnostics. A predicate that some build could satisfy, such as `cfg(feature = "x")`, `cfg(test)`, `cfg(windows)` or `all(unix, windows)`, keeps the gap. Discharging those through the build's selected cfg is #11834.

`brokk_bifrost_rust::cfg::is_unsatisfiable` is new. It answers a question about the predicate alone, so it does not depend on a selected atom set. Review pointed out that the producer calls it for every cfg-gated module, so it is bounded and does not recurse:
- It keeps only the nodes and atoms that are reachable after constant simplification.
- It answers "not proven" above 12 distinct atoms or 4096 nodes. "Not proven" keeps the gap, which is the fail-closed answer.
- Within the bound, it evaluates one bit-parallel truth table per node, in node order. The formula builder pushes a node only after its operands.

The shared SAT search that site activation uses is unchanged.

## Cause (confirmed)

`crates/bifrost-rust/src/resolution.rs`, in the `mod_item` arm for a conditional module without a body. The persisted gap had origin code 13 (`[redacted]`) and frontier kind `Other`, with no inventory or named reasons. These were ruled out:
- file activity (`rust_file_activity.sql`);
- open-inventory gaps;
- alias-expansion refusal (an inline `#[cfg(any())] mod x { .. }` has no placement gap and already resolved).

## Levers

- Rust resolution bundle v134 -> v140 (`crates/bifrost-store/src/analyzer/store/resolution.rs`), because the producer's output for unchanged sources changes. v135 to v139 are reserved by #11272. No open PR holds a Rust bundle above v134.
- One ICFG provider token line, because a bundle epoch rotates both ICFG halves.
- Rulings came from the native-engine coordinator. There is no migration.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --check`.
- Clippy `-D warnings` on `bifrost-rust` and `bifrost-rust-analysis`, all targets.
- Nextest on the `bifrost-rust` and `bifrost-rust-analysis` libs: 1098 passed.
- `bifrost-tools` and `bifrost-store` filters `rust_selected_shadow|rust_crates|rust_unit_summaries`: 240 passed.
- `suite_cross_language` rust: 42 passed.
- `suite_semantic golden_resolution_facts`: 8 passed.

New hard-won tests:
- `std_types.rs` `[redacted]`: the issue case, red before the fix and green after.
- The control `[redacted]`: a feature-gated module keeps the gap.
- `cfg::tests::[redacted]`: contradictions up to 12 atoms are proven, 13 and 21 atoms are not, and satisfiable and unknown predicates are not.

Built on `origin/master` 097d7939f5.

{"repo":"brokkai/mjolnir","kind":"issue","number":1495,"title":"Nitro sessions: host-path mounts and shared mbx build cache","body":"Follow-up to #1494.

Nitro Sandbox sessions (Firecracker microVMs) start without user-configured host-path mounts and without the shared mbx build cache, because Firecracker has no virtio-fs. The session reports this when it is created. The first version gives each VM only its own disks: the root clone plus named volumes for the workspace and /tmp.

Restoring both matters most for build speed on EC2 hosts, where the mbx cache lives on instance-store NVMe.

Candidate approach: the host serves each mount to exactly one guest over its point-to-point TAP link, for example with an NFSv4 export restricted to that guest's /30 address and enforced by the existing nftables table. The guest init mounts it at the destination. Needs measurement: whether mbx's cache locking and performance hold up over NFS, and the read-only versus copy-on-write semantics for additional mounts.
","author":"jbellis","url":"https://github.com/BrokkAi/mjolnir/issues/1495"}

{"repo":"brokkai/mjolnir","kind":"issue","number":1496,"title":"Docker and Podman inside Nitro Sandbox sessions","body":"Follow-up to #1494. Related to #1493.

Let the agent in a Nitro Sandbox session run containers with `docker` and `podman`, e.g. databases for tests, testcontainers, or building images. Ordinary Podman sessions cannot do this today: the agent-dev image's `podman` is `podman-remote`, which has no socket in a session. A microVM can offer it safely because containers run against the guest's own kernel, not the host's.

The #1494 spike showed rootless Podman working as the image user inside a guest (`podman run --rm alpine echo ok`, including outbound HTTPS). It needed:
- `podman crun uidmap fuse-overlayfs passt` in the image;
- `cgroup_manager="cgroupfs"`, since the guest has no systemd;
- `/dev/net/tun` and `/dev/fuse` set to mode 0666, and `/` made rshared, in the guest init;
- the overlay, fuse and tun kernel modules.

Details are in `.agents/docs/nitro-sandbox-spike.md`, "Nested containers".

To decide:
- Docker (dockerd inside the guest, probably rootful, since the VM is the boundary) as well as Podman. Rootful networking needs the bridge, veth and netfilter modules, which are loaded but untested.
- Where the engine comes from: the agent-dev image (which grows every session's image), a per-session opt-in, or a devcontainer feature once #1493 lands. For devcontainer images, #1493's `features` such as docker-in-docker would be the natural way to ask for it.
- Delegating a cgroup subtree to the image user, so `--memory`/`--cpus` work on nested containers.
- The `podman` command name: today it points at `podman-remote`, which daemons running inside the image rely on.
","author":"jbellis","url":"https://github.com/BrokkAi/mjolnir/issues/1496"}
